candidates.refactoringInfo: Move method printFailures to class TextListener
candidates.description:
Move method printFailures to org.junit.internal.TextListener
Rationale: The method printFailures() is responsible for printing the details of test failures, which directly relates to the functionality of the TextListener class. This class already handles how failures are printed through the printFailure() method. Moving printFailures() to TextListener will enhance cohesion by ensuring that all failure reporting logic is encapsulated within the same class. Additionally, since printFailures() utilizes the getWriter() method from TextListener to output messages, it logically fits within this class, making it more maintainable and easier to understand.

candidates.refactoringInfo: Move method printFooter to class TextListener
candidates.description:
Move method printFooter to org.junit.internal.TextListener
Rationale: The printFooter() method is responsible for displaying the results of a test run, including success and failure messages. Since TextListener already handles output related to test results, moving this method to it would encapsulate all test result-related functionality within the TextListener class. This promotes better cohesion, as TextListener would manage both the header and footer of the test output, streamlining the responsibilities of the class. Additionally, the method relies on the getWriter() method from TextListener, which makes it a natural fit for this class.

candidates.refactoringInfo: Move method runProtected to class Protectable
candidates.description:
Move method runProtected to junit.framework.Protectable
Rationale: The method runProtected() is designed to execute the protect() method from the Protectable interface, indicating a strong relationship with this class. It handles the execution of a Protectable instance and manages exceptions that may arise during its execution. Moving this method to Protectable aligns with the principle of encapsulating behavior related to protecting method execution, thus improving cohesion within the Protectable interface.

candidates.refactoringInfo: Move method run to class TestCase
candidates.description:
Move method run to junit.framework.TestCase
Rationale: The method 'run(TestCase test)' is inherently designed to execute a test case, which aligns perfectly with the responsibilities of the TestCase class. Since TestCase already has methods for setting up, tearing down, and running tests, moving 'run' here will encapsulate the test execution logic within the class that represents a single test case. This will enhance cohesion by keeping all methods related to test execution within the TestCase class, thus following the Single Responsibility Principle.

candidates.refactoringInfo: Move method addError to class Test

Moving this method to the Test class also enhances the readability and maintainability of the code, making it clearer that error handling is a responsibility of the Test itself.

candidates.description:
Move method evaluate2 to org.junit.internal.runners.statements.ExpectException
Rationale: The method evaluate2(ExpectException expectException) is designed to handle exception evaluation logic in the context of expected exceptions. It closely interacts with the ExpectException class, particularly in how it checks for expected exceptions during evaluation. Moving this method to the ExpectException class allows for better encapsulation of exception handling logic specific to the expectations set by this class. Additionally, the existing evaluate method in ExpectException already calls evaluate2, indicating a direct relationship between the two. This move would enhance code organization and maintainability by keeping related functionality together.
